attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Medical Genetics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Hearing difficulty noted since infancy

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
His parents report that he does not always respond when called and has been using sign language at school. They also note that he was born with unusually pale blue eyes of different shades and a patch of white hair near the forehead that has been present since birth. He has no history of recurrent ear infections, head trauma, or meningitis. Developmental milestones apart from speech are appropriate.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Waardenburg syndrome type 2
- Congenital sensorineural hearing loss (bilateral, severe)
- Iris heterochromia
- Poliosis (white forelock)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Bilateral tympanostomy tube placement (age 2 years)
- Auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing under sedation (age 6 months)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Vitamin D supplementation 600 IU oral daily
- Fluoride supplement 0.25 mg oral daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother with sensorineural hearing loss and premature graying
- Maternal grandfather with congenital heterochromia
- Paternal uncle with renal cell carcinoma (diagnosed age 42)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Preschool student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Physical examination shows striking heterochromia of the irises, a depigmented forelock, and mild lateral displacement of the inner canthi without visual impairment. No other craniofacial anomalies or cardiac murmurs are present.

OTHER STUDIES:
Audiometry confirms bilateral sensorineural hearing loss.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Mass noticed while bathing

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 6-year-old male with Waardenburg syndrome type 2, previously evaluated by Medical Genetics, presents with a mass. He has been eating and playing normally with no fever, vomiting, or behavioral changes and has no history of urinary symptoms or recent illnesses.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- PHACE syndrome (screening indicated) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Waardenburg syndrome type 2
- Congenital sensorineural hearing loss (bilateral, severe)
- Iris heterochromia
- Poliosis (white forelock)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Bilateral tympanostomy tube placement (age 2 years)
- Auditory brainstem response (ABR) testing under sedation (age 6 months)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Vitamin D supplementation 600 IU oral daily
- Fluoride supplement 0.25 mg oral daily

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother with sensorineural hearing loss and premature graying
- Maternal grandfather with congenital heterochromia
- Paternal uncle with renal cell carcinoma (diagnosed age 42)

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Preschool student.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
On further review of systems, the child has partial iris hypoplasia and a history of cryptorchidism.

VITAL SIGNS:
Stable vital signs

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the child is well-appearing. Abdominal palpation reveals a non-tender, firm mass occupying the right flank. The rest of the exam is normal. His growth parameters are at the 50th percentile.
